elements.name: TextBox 15
elements.text: Success: held-out accuracy, macro-F1 and per-class errors, with no leakage.

elements.name: TextBox 16
elements.text:
What we understood
Task: label each object STAR or GALAXY from brightness in 5 bands plus shape. QSOs are in the data; we exclude them from the main model.
Why it matters: stars are point sources, galaxies are extended. Catalogues need clean labels at survey scale; manual labelling is impossible.
Why it is hard: faint galaxies look point-like, poor seeing blurs stars, and measurements are noisy.
Traps (measured): Dataset_29 has junk text and ±1e12 sentinels; in Dataset_24 redshift reveals the class.
What it really tests: cleaning, relevant features, leakage control and generalisation, not accuracy alone.
Secondary check: a 5-band colour model trained on Dataset_29 fell from macro-F1 0.968 to 0.478 on 62,128 Dataset_24 objects: cross-survey transfer is a known limit.

notes.text:
SAY: This is our reading of the problem statement. Stars are point sources; galaxies have extent, but faint galaxies blur into points. The statement warns about unnecessary attributes, confusing measurements, unusual observations, bias and leakage, so we treat this as a data-quality and honesty problem. Our audit found junk text and sentinels in Dataset_29 and a label-revealing column (redshift) in both files. Dataset_24 was NOT used as training data; it was a secondary transfer check, and the drop from 0.968 to 0.478 macro-F1 shows we do not claim cross-survey generalisation.
KEY CLAIM: the raw data cannot be modelled as-is.
EVIDENCE: data audit numbers (measured) and the transfer check.

elements.name: TextBox 10
elements.text:
Data preparation
Clean: invalid text, non-finite and out-of-bound values become NaN (Dataset_29).
Drop: IDs, coordinates, observation bookkeeping, spectral type, galaxy-population fields.
Classes: star vs galaxy; 10,439 QSO excluded.
Duplicates: identity matching removed 37 unidentifiable rows and 126 conflicting-label rows, and collapsed 197 repeats: 100,050 → 89,251.
Missing values: median fill, learned inside each training fold.
Leakage: redshift excluded (stars sit at |z| < 0.005).

elements.name: TextBox 11
elements.text:
Features, model, evaluation
Features: 30 measurements plus 30 derived = 60 inputs: 5 colours, 5 PSF-minus-magnitude, 5 radius ratios, 10 log radii, 5 asinh fluxes.
Model: Histogram Gradient Boosting (HistGB_deeper), compared with a logistic-regression baseline.
Validation: 80/20 split (71,401 development, 17,850 test), five-fold CV; only the chosen model touched the test set.
Selection: permutation importance: drop in macro-F1 when an input is shuffled.
Metrics: accuracy, macro-F1, confusion matrix.

elements.name: TextBox 13
elements.text: Vs conventional: a single morphology or colour cut, versus an audited, leakage-checked pipeline validated by cross-validation.

notes.text:
SAY: Three parts: clean and audit the data, keep stars and galaxies only with repeated objects collapsed, then train a Histogram Gradient Boosting model on 60 inputs validated with five-fold CV on 71,401 development rows and scored once on 17,850 held-out objects. Redshift is excluded because it nearly gives the label for stars.
CAUTION: the radius ratio is Petrosian radius / half-light radius, not the conventional R90/R50 concentration, and the band magnitudes were not verified as model/cmodel magnitudes. Say so if asked.
KEY CLAIM: a leakage-free pipeline gives a score we can defend.
EVIDENCE: held-out accuracy 99.48%, macro-F1 0.9946 (slide 4).

elements.name: TextBox 34
elements.text:
Why this model fits
Beats baseline: CV macro-F1 up 0.29 points over logistic regression, a small but measured gain.
Rich inputs: colours, PSF-minus-magnitude and radius ratios capture point-like vs extended.
Balanced errors: 60 galaxies called stars, 33 stars called galaxies.
Leakage-safe: redshift, IDs and coordinates excluded; repeated objects collapsed.
Known limit: transfer to Dataset_24 was weak (macro-F1 0.478).

elements.name: TextBox 35
elements.text: Add: feature-importance chart and actual-vs-predicted plot (images needed). [TEAM]

notes.text:
SAY: Walk the seven steps. Final model HistGB_deeper: five-fold CV macro-F1 0.9946 vs 0.9918 for logistic regression (a 0.29-point gain), then 99.48% accuracy and 0.9946 macro-F1 on 17,850 held-out objects: 10,383 galaxies and 7,374 stars correct, 60 galaxies called stars, 33 stars called galaxies (93 errors). Only the chosen model touched the test set.
PIPELINE: 1 Load Dataset_29. 2 Inspect. 3 Clean: bad text and out-of-bound values to NaN, drop IDs/coordinates/bookkeeping/spectral fields, drop QSO and redshift, collapse repeated objects (100,050 to 89,251). 4 Build 30 derived features (60 inputs). 5 Split 80/20 (71,401 / 17,850). 6 Median-fill inside each fold, five-fold CV, pick HistGB_deeper. 7 Evaluate on test, permutation importance for interpretation. Output: probability per object; near 0.5 goes to follow-up.
HONEST LIMIT: a separate 5-band colour model scored macro-F1 0.968 on Dataset_29 holdout but 0.478 on Dataset_24, so we do not claim cross-survey generalisation.
KEY CLAIM: the model generalises to unseen Dataset_29 objects.
EVIDENCE: CV table, held-out metrics, confusion matrix (measured).

notes.text:
SAY: Real-world application. Rubin's LSST expects about 20 billion galaxies and 17 billion stars, far beyond manual labelling. The table shows astronomy-related market segments from analyst reports and government figures; estimates differ by report and are not independently verified, so quote them as ranges. Our classifier is a small piece of that data-analysis pipeline. Future scope: calibration and uncertainty, QSO as a third class, other surveys, rare-object detection.
KEY CLAIM: automated star-galaxy classification is needed at survey scale.
EVIDENCE: Rubin project figures; market-research estimates (caveat).
